model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_stor.name: stg_stores
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_stor.description:
Raw retail store dataset containing location, operational, and infrastructure
attributes. Profiling identified inconsistent state representations, malformed
phone numbers, invalid ZIP codes and heterogeneous boolean encodings for
operational flags. The staging model preserves source attributes while
enabling store-level standardization.

store_id.name: store_id
store_id.description:
Unique store identifier used as the primary key for store-level joins and
operational reporting.

store_name.name: store_name
store_name.description:
Store display name. Profiling applied title-case normalization and minimum
length checks to remove malformed values.

state.name: state
state.description:
Raw state attribute from the store source feed. Profiling found mixed
full-name and abbreviated values; downstream transformations produce
`state`-normalized columns (`state_full`, `state_abbr`) for analytical use.

zip_code.name: zip_code
zip_code.description:
Store ZIP/postal code. Profiling identified non-numeric values and
invalid lengths; numeric validation and length checks are applied during
standardization.

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_prod.name: stg_products
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_prod.description:
Raw product master dataset as ingested into the Bronze layer. Profiling
found malformed product identifiers, inconsistent SKU casing and formats,
mixed pricing representations, and variable availability encodings. This
staging model preserves source attributes while applying light structural
normalization to enable downstream product standardization.

product_id.name: product_id
product_id.description:
Unique product-level business identifier. Profiling identified malformed
and non-numeric product_id values; defensive integer conversion is
recommended. This field is expected to be the primary business key for
product-level joins.

sku.name: sku
sku.description:
Stock-keeping unit identifier. Source SKUs may contain inconsistent casing,
leading/trailing whitespace, and variable lengths. Upstream profiling
normalized SKUs to uppercase and trimmed patterns to improve joinability.

product_name.name: product_name
product_name.description:
Standardized product name after title-case normalization and whitespace
cleanup. Source product names exhibited inconsistent formatting and
partial truncation.

base_price_usd.name: base_price_usd
base_price_usd.description:
Base selling price expressed in USD. Profiling identified currency symbols,
thousands separators, negative values and malformed decimals; defensive
numeric parsing was applied downstream.

cost_price_usd.name: cost_price_usd
cost_price_usd.description:
Product cost price in USD. Used for margin analysis; profiling flagged
mismatches versus transaction-level cost references. Consumers should
reconcile with silver-level product pricing where available.

is_available.name: is_available
is_available.description:
Inventory / availability indicator sourced from product feeds. Profiling
consolidated numerous availability encodings into a small set of
canonical values (Available / Not Available / Discontinued / Unknown).

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_revi.name: stg_reviews
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_revi.description:
Raw customer review dataset containing ratings, review text, and engagement
metrics. Profiling found inconsistent rating encodings, malformed dates,
mixed verification indicators and duplicate review identifiers which must
be handled downstream.

review_id.name: review_id
review_id.description:
Unique review identifier. Profiling detected duplicates and structural
anomalies; deduplication and structural validation are required downstream.

rating.name: rating
rating.description:
Numeric customer rating. Profiling determined the accepted business range
is 1 through 5; values outside this range were nullified or flagged.

verified_purchase.name: verified_purchase
verified_purchase.description:
Purchase verification indicator (raw). Profiling normalized multiple
boolean-like encodings ('1','0','yes','no','verified') into canonical
values; downstream layers perform the mapping to 'Verified' / 'Not Verified' / 'Unknown'.

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_inve.name: stg_inventory
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_inve.description:
Staging model for inventory snapshot data. Profiling identified mixed date
formats, malformed product identifiers, negative stock quantities and
inconsistent warehouse mappings. The model includes a generated surrogate
key to represent inventory snapshot grain.

inventory_snapshot_sk.name: inventory_snapshot_sk
inventory_snapshot_sk.description:
Generated surrogate key for inventory snapshot grain derived from
snapshot_date, product_id and store_id. This key is deterministic and
intended to provide a stable row identifier for deduplication and
joins.

snapshot_date.name: snapshot_date
snapshot_date.description:
Inventory snapshot date normalized to ISO 8601. Profiling showed mixed
regional date formats; conditional parsing and defensive handling were
applied during standardization.

product_id.name: product_id
product_id.description:
Product identifier referenced in inventory snapshots. Profiling identified
malformed and non-numeric product IDs; downstream validation against the
product dimension is recommended.

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_inve.raw_code:
SELECT
    {{ dbt_utils.generate_surrogate_key([
        'snapshot_date',
        'product_id',
        'store_id'
    ]) }} AS inventory_snapshot_sk,

    snapshot_date,
    product_id,
    product_name,
    sku,
    category,
    stock_on_hand,
    stock_reserved,
    stock_available,
    reorder_level,
    unit_cost,
    unit_price,
    inventory_value,
    warehouse_location,
    store_id

FROM {{ source('bronze', 'inventory_snapshots') }};
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_inve.compiled_code:

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_cust.name: stg_customers
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_cust.description:
Staging model for the customer master dataset that exposes raw customer
information from the Bronze layer in a standardized dbt model structure.
This model preserves the original source values without applying business
transformations or data cleansing. Its primary purpose is to provide a
consistent interface for downstream models while documenting the data
quality issues identified during source profiling at the column level.
Data standardization, validation, and business rule implementation are
intentionally deferred to subsequent transformation layers.

customer_id.name: customer_id
customer_id.description:
Unique customer identifier sourced from the customer master table. This field
serves as the primary business key or surrogate key used to uniquely identify
customer records across source and downstream systems. The value is expected
to be unique and non-null for all records, ensuring entity integrity and
supporting reliable customer-level analysis, data integration, and reporting.

title.name: title
title.description:
Customer title or honorific prefix (for example, NULL,Dr.,Mr.,Mrs.,Ms.,Prof.)
sourced from customer master data. This field contain leading and
trailing whitespace, inconsistent formatting, capitalization variations, and
null values. Standardization is required to ensure consistent reporting
and downstream data consumption.

first_name.name: first_name
first_name.description:
Customer first name captured from source customer records. This field 
contain leading and trailing whitespace, inconsistent capitalization, null
values, and formatting discrepancies. In certain cases, the value not
align with the corresponding component of full_name due to data quality
issues, source system inconsistencies, or manual entry errors.

last_name.name: last_name
last_name.description:
Customer last name captured from source customer records. This field 
contain leading and trailing whitespace, inconsistent capitalization, null
values, and formatting discrepancies. Some records  exhibit mismatches
between last_name and the surname component extracted from full_name due to
source data quality issues or inconsistent customer master records.

full_name.name: full_name
full_name.description:
Customer full name derived from source customer records. This field contain
leading and trailing whitespace, inconsistent capitalization, formatting
variations, and data quality issues. In some records, the value not align
with the concatenated combination of title, first_name, and last_name due to
source system inconsistencies, data entry errors, or incomplete customer
information. Data validation and standardization should be applied to ensure
consistency across customer identity attributes.

gender.name: gender
gender.description:
Customer gender information captured from source customer records. This field
exhibits data quality challenges including null values, leading and trailing
whitespace, inconsistent capitalization, and non-standardized gender
representations. Equivalent gender categories stored in multiple
formats (e.g., 'F', 'Female', 'FEMALE', 'M', 'Male', 'MALE', 'NB',
'Non-Binary', 'Other', and 'Prefer not to say'). Data cleansing and
normalization should be applied to establish a consistent set of gender
values for analytical and reporting purposes.

date_of_birth.name: date_of_birth
date_of_birth.description:
Customer date of birth captured from source customer records. This field
contains multiple date formats, mixed regional date conventions, locale
ambiguity, inconsistent separators, malformed date values, and ambiguous
month/day ordering. Source values were profiled, classified, and standardized
into ISO date format using pattern-based parsing and error-handling logic.
Ambiguous dates were resolved according to dataset-level format analysis and
established business rules to support consistent analytical reporting and
downstream data consumption.

age.name: age
age.description:
Customer age attribute captured from source records. Source values
contain missing data, invalid ages, and inconsistencies with the associated
date_of_birth value. For analytical consistency, age should be derived from
the standardized date_of_birth field rather than relying on the raw source
attribute, ensuring accurate customer demographic reporting and segmentation.

email.name: email
email.description:
Customer email address captured from source customer records. Source values
contain inconsistent casing, leading and trailing whitespace, malformed
email structures, duplicate '@' symbols, domain spelling errors, and other
invalid representations. Email values were standardized through case
normalization, whitespace removal, domain correction, and structural
validation to ensure consistent customer identification, communication, and
downstream analytical reporting.

phone.name: phone
phone.description:
Customer phone number captured from source customer records. Source values
contain inconsistent formatting, structural variations, invalid digit
groupings, incomplete phone numbers, and malformed representations. Phone
numbers were profiled, parsed, validated, and standardized into the canonical
US format '+1 (AAA) BBB-CCCC'. Records failing structural validation were
flagged as invalid to ensure consistent customer contact information and
downstream analytical reporting.

address.name: address
address.description:
Customer street address captured from source customer records. Source values
contain inconsistent formatting, structural variations, and wrong address information.
and This field contain leading and trailing whitespace.

city.name: city
city.description:
Customer city name captured from source customer records. Source values
contain inconsistent formatting, structural variations, incomplete address
 information, and malformed representations.
City values were profiled, parsed, validated, and standardized into the
canonical US format 'Anytown'. Records failing structural validation were
flagged as invalid to ensure consistent customer address information and
downstream analytical reporting.

state.name: state
state.description:
Customer state name captured from source customer records. Source values 
contain full-state names, inconsistent capitalization, misspellings, and
mixed representations (abbreviations vs full names). During profiling the
state attribute was found to be semantically redundant relative to the
derived and standardized `state_abbr` and `state_full` attributes maintained
in the final model. Downstream workflows should prefer `state_abbr` or
`state_full` for reliable geographic joins and reporting; `state` is retained
here to preserve source-system fidelity but contain malformed or
inconsistent values.

state_abbr.name: state_abbr
state_abbr.description:
Canonical two-letter U.S. state abbreviation derived from the source `state`
attribute. Values were normalized to uppercase two-character abbreviations
(for example, 'CA', 'TX', 'NY'). Profiling identified mixed input formats and
misspellings; transformation logic defensively maps known variants and
leaves unknown values null to avoid incorrect geographic attribution.

state_full.name: state_full
state_full.description:
Canonical full-state name (for example, 'California', 'Texas', 'New York')
derived from the source `state` attribute. This column is normalized to
title case and used for human-readable reporting where full names are
preferred.

zip_code.name: zip_code
zip_code.description:
Postal code / ZIP code captured from source customer records. Profiling
identified non-numeric characters, incorrect lengths, and missing values.
The transformation includes numeric validation and minimum-length checks;
malformed values are flagged as invalid or nullified depending on severity.

country.name: country
country.description:
Customer country attribute standardized to common country names (for example,
('United States'). Profiling detected mixed abbreviations ('US', 'USA', 'U.S.'),
inconsistent casing, and missing values. The canonical value is used for
regional analysis and currency assumptions.

region.name: region
region.description:
Higher-level regional classification derived from geographic attributes
(for example, 'West', 'South', 'Midwest', etc.). Region values were computed from
standardized state information and used to support aggregated regional
analysis. Records with unresolved state mappings may have null region values.

customer_segment.name: customer_segment
customer_segment.description:
Customer segmentation attribute (for example, Bronze, Gold, Platinum, Silver).
Profiling revealed inconsistent category labels and legacy codes; the
transformation maps common variants to a small canonical set and preserves
unknown values for later review.

loyalty_points.name: loyalty_points
loyalty_points.description:
Numeric loyalty program balance captured from source systems. Profiling
identified negative and non-numeric representations; defensive numeric
parsing and non-negative enforcement were applied. Invalid values are
nullified to prevent incorrect downstream aggregations.

is_active.name: is_active
is_active.description:
Operational indicator reflecting whether the customer account is currently
active. Source values used heterogeneous boolean encodings (for example,
'1', '0', 'Y', 'N', 'true', 'false', etc.). Transformation normalizes values to
True / False / Unknown categories to support active-customer analyses.

account_created_date.name: account_created_date
account_created_date.description:
ISO-standardized timestamp representing when the customer account was created.
Profiling identified mixed date formats and timezone ambiguity; values were
parsed using pattern-aware parsing logic with invalid or ambiguous dates
nullified rather than imputed.

preferred_channel.name: preferred_channel
preferred_channel.description:
Customer's preferred contact or marketing channel (for example, APP, Catalog,
in-store, Mobile App, Online, Web, etc.). Profiling showed semantic drift and varied
abbreviations; mapping rules consolidate the dominant variants into a
controlled vocabulary.

annual_income_usd.name: annual_income_usd
annual_income_usd.description:
Customer annual income expressed in USD. Profiling identified currency
symbol contamination, comma separators, and negative or non-numeric values.
Defensive currency parsing and non-negative enforcement were applied; invalid
representations are nullified to avoid skewing income-based segmentations.

company.name: company
company.description:
Customer company affiliation when provided. Values were profiled for
inconsistent casing, abbreviations, and truncation; transformation includes
whitespace cleanup and title-case normalization.

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_empl.name: stg_employees
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_empl.description:
Raw employee master dataset containing identity, contact, organizational,
compensation and managerial attributes. Profiling surfaced malformed emails,
inconsistent phone formats, mixed date ecosystems, and invalid numeric
compensation values. This staging model preserves source attributes for
downstream normalization.

employee_id.name: employee_id
employee_id.description:
Unique employee identifier used for joinability with transaction and
store tables. Profiling validated this identifier as the natural key and
recommended enforcing uniqueness at downstream stages.

first_name.name: first_name
first_name.description:
Customer first name captured from source customer records. This field
contains inconsistent casing (mixed uppercase, lowercase, and title case),
leading and trailing whitespace, and formatting discrepancies. Profiling 
identified no null values, ensuring complete coverage for this attribute.
Standardization and whitespace trimming are required to establish a 
consistent format for downstream analytical reporting and personalization.

last_name.name: last_name
last_name.description:
Employee last name captured from source records. This field exhibits 
inconsistent casing, including mixed uppercase, lowercase, and title case 
representations, as well as leading and trailing whitespace. Profiling 
confirms there are no null values in this field. Standardizing the 
casing and removing whitespace is required to ensure reliable 
employee-level identification and reporting in downstream models.

full_name.name: full_name
full_name.description:
Employee full name derived from concatenated source records. This field 
contains inconsistent casing (mixed uppercase, lowercase, and title case) 
and significant leading and trailing whitespace. To ensure data 
consistency for reporting and directory services, this field is 
standardized through whitespace removal and title-case normalization. 
It serves as a primary display attribute, and its alignment with 
the individual `first_name` and `last_name` components is verified to 
ensure identity accuracy.

email.name: email
email.description:
Employee email address captured from source records. Profiling identified
significant data quality challenges, including malformed domain structures,
duplicate '@' symbols, and inconsistent casing (mixed uppercase and 
lowercase). To ensure data integrity, defensive cleaning—including 
case normalization, whitespace trimming, and structural pattern validation—is 
applied during downstream transformations to facilitate reliable internal 
communications and employee identification.

phone.name: phone
phone.description:
Employee contact phone number. Source data contains highly inconsistent 
formatting, including varied separators (dots, hyphens, parentheses) and 
missing area codes or digit groupings. To ensure reliable contact 
information, all values are parsed, validated, and normalized into the 
canonical US format '+1 (AAA) BBB-CCCC'. Records that fail to meet this 
structure are flagged as invalid to maintain high data quality for 
downstream reporting and operational use.

job_title.name: job_title
job_title.description:
Official employee job title. This field is highly standardized, 
featuring consistent title-case formatting with no leading or 
trailing whitespace. Data profiling confirms that these values are 
clean and ready for immediate use in organizational reporting, 
resource allocation, and workforce analytics without the need for 
further transformation.

department.name: department
department.description:
Organizational department classification. The values in this field are 
well-structured, adhering to consistent title-case formatting with 
no leading or trailing whitespace. The data is validated as clean, 
reliable, and ready for direct use in downstream workforce segmentation 
and departmental reporting.

store_id.name: store_id
store_id.description:
Unique identifier for the retail store where the employee is currently 
assigned. This field is consistently formatted and requires no 
cleansing or structural transformation. Please note that this column 
naturally contains duplicate values, as multiple employees are assigned 
to the same store location. It is suitable for use as a foreign key 
when joining with the stores dimension for operational or regional 
reporting[cite: 1].

store_name.name: store_name
store_name.description:
Official retail store display name. The data is well-structured and 
follows consistent title-case formatting, requiring no cleansing. 
The values incorporate store location and format identifiers (e.g., 
'Flagship', 'Express', 'Pop-Up', 'Outlet', 'Standard'). As a 
standardized dimension, this field is reliable for store-level 
aggregation and performance comparison across different store tiers.

store_city.name: store_city
store_city.description:
The city location of the retail store where the employee is assigned. 
The data is presented in a clean, standardized format, utilizing 
consistent title-case capitalization with no leading or trailing 
whitespace. This field is reliable for geographic filtering and 
regional store-performance analysis without requiring further 
transformation.

hire_date.name: hire_date
hire_date.description:
Employee hire date captured from source systems. The raw data exhibits 
significant complexity, including multiple date formats, varied 
regional conventions (e.g., month/day ordering), inconsistent 
separators, and full-text month naming variations. To ensure 
analytical integrity, these values have been parsed, validated, and 
normalized into the ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DD). Ambiguous dates were 
resolved using pattern-based parsing and established business logic to 
support reliable downstream temporal analysis and workforce reporting.

years_employed.name: years_employed
years_employed.description:
Employee tenure represented as a numeric value. The current integer 
format fails to capture fractional periods, such as employees with 
partial-year experience (e.g., 6 years and 7 months). Additionally, 
profiling indicates that values for inactive employees are inconsistent 
or inaccurate. This column is being refactored to a decimal (float) 
format to ensure precision for tenure-based reporting, and validation 
logic is being implemented to correct calculations for both active and 
inactive personnel.

annual_salary_usd.name: annual_salary_usd
annual_salary_usd.description:
Annual base salary of the employee expressed in USD. The data is 
clean, consistently formatted as integers, and requires no structural 
transformation or cleansing. This field is validated for accuracy 
and is ready for immediate use in compensation analysis, budgeting, 
and workforce cost reporting.

commission_rate_pct.name: commission_rate_pct
commission_rate_pct.description:
Employee commission rate expressed as a percentage. The source data 
contains mixed numeric types (integers and decimals) due to 
inconsistent formatting across systems. To ensure mathematical 
accuracy for payroll and performance incentive calculations, this 
field is cast to a uniform decimal data type. No additional 
categorical or structural transformation is required; the focus 
is solely on maintaining precision for commission-based reporting.

is_active.name: is_active
is_active.description:
Operational status indicator reflecting whether an employee is currently 
active within the organization. The source data contains heterogeneous 
encodings, including boolean-like values ('1', 'Y', 'Yes'), negative 
indicators ('N', 'No'), and status descriptors ('Active', 'Terminated'). 
To support consistent workforce analysis, this field is normalized to a 
standard boolean (True/False) format. All ambiguous or non-standard 
representations are mapped during transformation to ensure reliable 
reporting on headcount and active personnel.

performance_rating.name: performance_rating
performance_rating.description:
Employee performance appraisal rating. Profiling identified significant
inconsistencies, including a mix of numeric grades (2-5), character 
grades (A-D), and descriptive text (e.g., 'Excellent', 'Average'). 
Additionally, missing values are currently represented by nulls or 
inconsistent labels. This field requires a standardization mapping 
to a uniform scale, with 'Unknown' used as the canonical value for 
missing or invalid records to ensure reliable performance-based 
segmentation and talent analytics.

manager_id.name: manager_id
manager_id.description:
Identifier of the employee's direct supervisor. The data is largely 
consistent; however, this field contains null values for top-level 
management or executive roles, as these individuals do not report to 
another manager within the organizational hierarchy. This column is 
suitable for use in recursive queries or self-joins to map the 
reporting structure and organizational tree.

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_tran.name: stg_transactions
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_tran.description:
Raw sales transaction dataset preserving source-level order, customer,
product, store and employee attributes. Profiling exposed multi-format dates,
currency-formatted numeric strings, negative financial values, duplicate
transaction identifiers and inconsistent categorical encodings. This staging
model mirrors the Bronze input and serves as the ingestion point for
chronological and financial standardization.

transaction_id.name: transaction_id
transaction_id.description:
Raw transaction identifier originating from source systems. Profiling
identified duplicate `transaction_id` values in the Bronze layer; deduplication
occurs downstream. This field should be considered the primary identifier
for transaction records within this model.

order_line_number.name: order_line_number
order_line_number.description:
Line number within the parent order. Profiling enforced a valid business
range (1-20) and flagged out-of-range values as invalid. This column is
used as part of the compound key with `transaction_id` at later stages.

customer_id.name: customer_id
customer_id.description:
Customer reference captured with the transaction. Profiling detected nulls
and orphaned values; referential validation against the customers dimension
is performed in downstream layers.

product_id.name: product_id
product_id.description:
Product reference associated with the transaction. Profiling identified
malformed and null product references; downstream joins to product
dimensions are used for validation and cross-checking.

unit_list_price.name: unit_list_price
unit_list_price.description:
Catalog price field captured as a source string. Profiling found currency
symbols and thousands separators; downstream cleaning converts this to a
decimal USD representation.

line_total_with_tax.name: line_total_with_tax
line_total_with_tax.description:
Final line total including tax. Profiling performed cross-validation with
recalculated totals derived from quantity and unit pricing; discrepancies
were flagged for corrective logic in the Silver layer.

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_retu.name: stg_returns
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.stg_retu.description:
Raw returns dataset containing return events and refund metadata. Profiling
revealed heterogeneous return channels, malformed identifiers, inconsistent
monetary formats, and missing product/customer references. This staging
model preserves the source-level return events and supports downstream
refund and return reconciliation.

return_id.name: return_id

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.int_inve.name: int_inventory_stock
model.dbt_analytics_engineering.int_inve.description:
Calculates key physical unit availability metrics across inventory snapshots by enforcing 
numeric boundaries. The model validates system counts, filters out impossible negative numbers, 
and computes real-time pickable availability balances to provide an accurate picture of net warehouse stock.

stock_reserved.description:
The count of units allocated or committed to active customer orders. 
Negative entries or invalid numeric data strings are coerced to NULL.

stock_available.name: stock_available
stock_available.description:
The net quantity of items currently pickable, sellable, and uncommitted. 
**Transformation Logic:** Dynamically calculated inline as `stock_on_hand` minus `stock_reserved`.

or registering below zero are converted to NULL.

WITH inventory as 
(
SELECT 
    inventory_snapshot_sk,

    CASE 
        WHEN TRY_CONVERT(INT, stock_on_hand) IS NULL OR TRY_CONVERT(INT, stock_on_hand) < 0 THEN NULL 
        ELSE TRY_CONVERT(INT, stock_on_hand)
    END AS stock_on_hand,

    CASE 
        WHEN TRY_CONVERT(INT, stock_reserved) < 0 OR TRY_CONVERT(INT, stock_reserved) IS NULL THEN NULL 
        ELSE TRY_CONVERT(INT, stock_reserved)
    END  as stock_reserved,

    CASE 
        WHEN TRY_CONVERT(INT, reorder_level) IS NULL OR TRY_CONVERT(INT, reorder_level) < 0 THEN NULL 
        ELSE TRY_CONVERT(INT, reorder_level)
    END as reorder_level
FROM {{ ref('stg_inventory') }}
)
SELECT 
    inventory_snapshot_sk,
    stock_on_hand,
    stock_reserved,
    stock_on_hand - stock_reserved AS  stock_available,
    reorder_level
FROM inventory;

unit_price.description:
The Manufacturer's Suggested Retail Price (MSRP) for the item, cast to a decimal(10,2) format. 
**Transformation Logic:** Cleanses text strings by stripping out both currency '$' characters
and embedded thousands comma groupings (',') to allow safe mathematical execution.

The physical count of units present in the warehouse. Non-numeric inputs or negative counts 
resolve to NULL to protect downstream multiplication.

inventory_value.name: inventory_value
inventory_value.description:
The extended total dollar value of the stock on hand. 
**Transformation Logic:** Evaluated dynamically by multiplying the cleaned `unit_price`
 by the validated `stock_on_hand`.

warehouse_location.description:
The tracking designation code for the storage facility. Values are standardized to UPPERCASE 
with missing or blank fields defaulting to 'Unknown'.

store_id.name: store_id

The associated brick-and-mortar retail location identifier. Converted to an integer data type, 
with missing or blank spaces coerced to NULL.

WITH inventory_valuation AS 
(
    SELECT 
        inventory_snapshot_sk,
        CASE 
            WHEN unit_cost LIKE '$%' THEN TRY_CONVERT(DECIMAL(10, 2), SUBSTRING(unit_cost, 2, LEN(unit_cost)))
            ELSE TRY_CONVERT(DECIMAL(10, 2), unit_cost)
        END as unit_cost,

        CASE 
            WHEN TRY_CONVERT(DECIMAL(10,2), unit_price) IS NULL THEN TRY_CONVERT(DECIMAL(10,2), REPLACE(REPLACE(unit_price, ',', ''), '$', ''))
            ELSE TRY_CONVERT(DECIMAL(10, 2), unit_price)
        END as unit_price,

        CASE 
            WHEN TRY_CONVERT(INT, stock_on_hand) IS NULL OR stock_on_hand < 0 THEN NULL 
            ELSE TRY_CONVERT(INT, stock_on_hand)
        END AS stock_on_hand,

        CASE 
            WHEN warehouse_location IS NULL OR warehouse_location = '' THEN 'Unknown'
            ELSE UPPER(warehouse_location)
        END as warehouse_location,

        CASE 
            WHEN store_id IS NULL OR store_id = '' THEN NULL
            ELSE TRY_CONVERT(INT, store_id)
        END as store_id 

    FROM {{ ref('stg_inventory') }}
)
SELECT 
    inventory_snapshot_sk,
    unit_cost,
    unit_price,
    unit_price * stock_on_hand as inventory_value,
    warehouse_location,
    store_id
FROM inventory_valuation;

headcount and cost center distribution analysis.

like 'X', 'AZ', 'N/A'), it is safely routed to `'Unknown'`. Otherwise, it strips extra whitespace.

annual_salary_usd.description:

**Transformation Logic:** Casts the incoming raw currency format to a high-precision decimal 
type `DECIMAL(18,2)` to preserve cents accuracy and protect against floating-point errors. 
Crucially, if the salary is non-numeric, null, or falls below zero (`< 0`), it is forced to 
`NULL` to avoid corrupting financial aggregates, averages, and budget metrics.

commission_rate_pct.description:

**Transformation Logic:** Casts values to a tight numeric decimal boundary of `DECIMAL(4,2)`

input vector containing numbers (`5`, `4`, `3`, `2`), letter grades (`A`, `B`, `C`, `D`), and

- *'False'* (Separated/Inactive status; mapped from: 'terminated', 'n', 'no', '0', 'false')

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.int_tran.description:
**Layer:** Silver / Intermediate (Supply Chain & Logistics Chronology)
**Core Objective:** Constructs an immutable timeline tracking order lifecycle milestones (Order -> Ship -> Deliver).
**Engineering Strategy:** Solves severe omni-channel system data quality issues. First, it implements a 
**Multi-Locale Temporal Parsing Ladder** to map text inputs into a unified `DATE` type. Second, it resolves supply chain 
logical anomalies—such as an item being marked shipped before it was bought, or an item marked delivered before it left 
the warehouse—by executing temporal delta matrices and data rotation logic.

order_date.name: order_date
order_date.description:
The foundational transaction generation calendar date.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Uses pattern matching (`LIKE`) to parse multiple text layout structures. 
It evaluates textual names (e.g., `Jan 01, 2026`) and splits ambiguous international vs. US layouts by validating component lengths 
and string thresholds before mapping to standard date conversion types (`101`, `103`, `105`, `110`).

ship_date.name: ship_date
ship_date.description:
The official date the package departed the distribution center.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Employs defensive supply chain chronology rules via `DATEDIFF`:
- If shipping occurs *before* `order_date` (negative window) or spans *greater than 15 days* (SLA breach), 
  the engine uses `DATEFROMPARTS` to fix reversed day/month inputs.
- If the value is completely unpopulated, it inserts an estimated corporate 
  logistics SLA timeline of `DATEADD(DAY, 7, order_date)`.

delivery_date.name: delivery_date
delivery_date.description:
The milestone date indicating successful logistics delivery at the destination address.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Processes delivery tracking anomalies via nested chronological filters:
- If the delivery occurs *greater than 17 days* post-shipment or registers an impossible negative window 
*less than -15 days prior to shipment*, it triggers an active component rearrangement to restore structural order timeline tracking.

shipping_method.name: shipping_method
shipping_method.description: The distribution courier tier option chosen (e.g., Standard Ground, Next-Day Air Express).

sales_channel.name: sales_channel
sales_channel.description: The touchpoint platform tracking where the purchase originated (e.g., Online Storefront, Mobile Application, Retail).

payment_method.name: payment_method
payment_method.description: The financial tender type used to settle the transaction ledger.

**Layer:** Silver / Intermediate (Financial Analytics Dimension)
**Core Objective:** Cleanses, standardizes, and calculates itemized financial metrics at the basket line item level.
**Engineering Strategy:** Implements an automated data quality firewall to sanitize text-polluted currency strings 
and protect downstream revenue dashboards from corrupt outliers. It shields metrics from calculation errors by 
applying a strict business rule bounding matrix. If an upstream element breaches logical rules or contains un-castable 
text artifacts, the engine performs a defensive coercion to `NULL` to keep the production processing pipeline alive.

transaction_id.name: transaction_id
transaction_id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying the internal item line ledger record.

quantity_ordered.name: quantity_ordered
quantity_ordered.description:
The volume of physical units committed to the purchase line item.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Restricts metrics to a realistic business scale using an explicit 
boundary conditional (`CASE WHEN quantity_ordered < 1 THEN NULL WHEN quantity_ordered > 30 THEN NULL ...`). 
Outliers are coerced to `NULL` to protect downstream calculations like Average Unit Retail (AUR).

unit_list_price.name: unit_list_price
unit_list_price.description:
The item sticker base MSRP.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Upstream ERP formats include strings with raw currency glyphs 
and formatting punctuation. The SQL engine strips characters via nested string manipulations 
(`REPLACE(REPLACE(unit_list_price, '$', ''), ',', '')`) before executing a high-precision `TRY_CONVERT(DECIMAL(10,2), ...)` operation.

discount_pct.name: discount_pct
discount_pct.description:
The authorized marketing markdown percentage applied to the item line.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Uses a guardrail condition to force entries between 0% and 100%. 
Corrupted negatives or values over 100% resolve to `NULL`, while valid decimals are truncated via `ROUND(discount_pct, 0)`.

line_total_before_tax.name: line_total_before_tax
line_total_before_tax.description:
Net transaction subtotal prior to government tax evaluation.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Sanitizes values by stripping currency text formatting, casting to `DECIMAL(10,2)`, 
and explicitly coercing impossible negative calculations (`< 0`) to `NULL`.

tax_rate_pct.name: tax_rate_pct
tax_rate_pct.description:
The registered state or regional tax percentage category.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Evaluated into a rounded `INT` structure. Standardized strictly between a 
0% minimum and 100% maximum scale to eliminate calculation errors.

tax_amount.name: tax_amount
tax_amount.description: The total absolute tax currency value applied to the ledger row. Stripped of structural text noise (`$`, `,`) and cast to `DECIMAL(10,2)`.

line_total_with_tax.name: line_total_with_tax
line_total_with_tax.description:
The final aggregate financial customer liability for the row line item.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Sanitized of currency characters and cast to a clean `DECIMAL(10,2)`. It includes a built-in business check: 
if the aggregate calculates below 0, it indicates data corruption and resolves to `NULL`.

            THEN NULL 

        ELSE TRY_CONVERT(DECIMAL(10, 2), REPLACE(REPLACE(unit_list_price, '$', ''), ',', '')) 
    END as unit_list_price,

    CASE 
        WHEN discount_pct IS NULL OR discount_pct < 0 OR discount_pct > 100 
            THEN NULL

    CASE

        ELSE TRY_CONVERT(DECIMAL(10,2), REPLACE(REPLACE(line_total_with_tax, '$', ''), ',', ''))

    tax_amount,

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.int_tran.description:
**Layer:** Silver / Intermediate (Categorical Status & Campaign Context Layer)
**Core Objective:** Standardizes alphanumeric operational states, status markers, marketing descriptors, and source system tags.
**Engineering Strategy:** Implements categorical smoothing to fix text fragmentation. It cleanses leading/trailing whitespace, 
normalizes mixed-case strings, removes hidden carriage returns, and consolidates fragmented system statuses into a uniform corporate taxonomy.

promo_id.name: promo_id
promo_id.description: Core tracking code link for the applied marketing promotion campaign.

promo_name.name: promo_name
promo_name.description:
Standardized label of the marketing campaign applied to the transaction.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Evaluates disparate user inputs and system text markers 
(`TRIM(LOWER(promo_name))`) into a standardized Title Case taxonomy (e.g., 'Winter Clearance', 'Bundle Deal', 'Flash Sale'). 
Unmapped campaign descriptors preserve their raw text layout but are cleaned of trailing whitespace.

order_status.name: order_status
order_status.description:
The normalized state tracking the operational milestone of the order lifecycle.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Translates fragmented system markers using an explicit taxonomy 
mapping tree. It forces character uniformity to standard options: 'Pending', 'Processing', 'Shipped', 'Delivered', 'Returned', or 'Cancelled'.

is_returned.name: is_returned
is_returned.description:
A clean boolean indicator identifying if an order line was returned post-purchase.
**Business Logic & SQL Mechanics:** Standardizes inconsistent system inputs (`yes`, `y`, `true`, `1`) into a 
uniform `'True'` category. Negative inputs resolve to `'False'`, and corrupted rows map safely to `'Unknown'`.

data_source.name: data_source
data_source.description:
A system tracking metric that records the source application of origin (e.g., 'CRM', 'Web'). 
This field is crucial for data lineage audits and root-cause error analysis.

model.dbt_analytics_engineering.int_tran.raw_code:
SELECT
    transaction_id,

    promo_id,

    CASE TRIM(LOWER(promo_name))
        WHEN 'winter clearance' THEN 'Winter Clearance'
        WHEN 'bundle deal'      THEN 'Bundle Deal'
        WHEN 'no promo'         THEN 'No Promo'
        WHEN 'flash sale'       THEN 'Flash Sale'
        WHEN 'black friday'     THEN 'Black Friday'
        WHEN 'holiday special'  THEN 'Holiday Special'
        WHEN 'weekend deal'     THEN 'Weekend Deal'
        WHEN 'loyalty reward'   THEN 'Loyalty Reward'
        WHEN 'cyber monday'     THEN 'Cyber Monday'
        ELSE TRIM(promo_name)
    END AS promo_name,

    CASE TRIM(LOWER(order_status))
        WHEN 'pending'    THEN 'Pending'
        WHEN 'processing' THEN 'Processing'
        WHEN 'shipped'    THEN 'Shipped'
        WHEN 'delivered'  THEN 'Delivered'
        WHEN 'returned'   THEN 'Returned'
        WHEN 'cancelled'  THEN 'Cancelled'
        ELSE TRIM(order_status)
    END AS order_status,

    CASE 
        WHEN TRIM(LOWER(is_returned)) IN ('yes', 'y', 'true', '1') 
            THEN 'True'

        WHEN TRIM(LOWER(is_returned)) IN ('no', 'n', 'false', '0') 
            THEN 'False'
            
        ELSE 'Unknown'
    END AS is_returned,

    CASE TRIM(LOWER(data_source))
        WHEN 'crm'    THEN 'CRM'
        WHEN 'web'    THEN 'Web'
        WHEN 'pos'    THEN 'POS'
        WHEN 'manual' THEN 'Manual'
        WHEN 'erp'    THEN 'ERP'
        ELSE 'Unknown'
    END AS data_source

FROM {{ ref('stg_transactions') }} ;

-- Model: int_customers_contact
--
-- Purpose:
--   Creates a trusted customer contact dataset by validating, correcting, and
--   standardizing customer communication attributes. This model repairs common
--   email formatting issues and domain typographical errors, transforms phone
--   numbers into a consistent business format, and normalizes preferred
--   communication channels into standardized business categories. The resulting
--   dataset provides reliable contact information for customer communication,
--   marketing campaigns, CRM operations, and downstream analytical models.
--
-- Maintainer: Ritik
-- ============================================================================
SELECT
    customer_id,

    CASE
        WHEN email IS NULL OR TRIM(email) = '' THEN 'Unknown'
        WHEN {{ trim_lower('email') }} NOT LIKE '%@%' 
            THEN 'Unknown'

        WHEN PATINDEX('%@%@%', {{ trim_lower('email') }}) > 0 
            THEN
                LEFT({{ trim_lower('email') }},CHARINDEX('@', {{ trim_lower('email') }}) - 1)
                + '@' +
                REPLACE(
                    SUBSTRING(
                        {{ trim_lower('email') }},
                        CHARINDEX('@', {{ trim_lower('email') }}) + 1,
                        LEN(email)),'@','')
        ELSE
            CONCAT(
                LEFT({{ trim_lower('email') }},CHARINDEX('@', {{ trim_lower('email') }}) - 1), '@',
                CASE
                    WHEN RIGHT(
                        {{ trim_lower('email') }},
                        LEN(TRIM(email)) - CHARINDEX('@', TRIM(email))) = 'yahoocom' THEN 'yahoo.com'

                    WHEN RIGHT(
                        {{ trim_lower('email') }},
                        LEN(TRIM(email)) - CHARINDEX('@', TRIM(email))) = 'iclod.com' THEN 'icloud.com'

                    WHEN RIGHT(
                        {{ trim_lower('email') }},

                        {{ trim_lower('email') }},

                    ELSE RIGHT(
                        {{ trim_lower('email') }},
                        LEN(TRIM(email)) - CHARINDEX('@', TRIM(email)))
                END
        )
    END AS email,
    
    {{ standardize_phone('phone') }}  as phone,

    CASE {{ trim_lower('preferred_channel') }}
        WHEN 'app'        THEN 'Mobile App'
        WHEN 'mobile app' THEN 'Mobile App'
        WHEN 'mobile'     THEN 'Mobile App'

macro.dbt_sqlserver.sqlserver__list_nonc.macro_sql:
{% macro sqlserver__list_nonclustered_rowstore_indexes(relation) -%}
  {% call statement('list_nonclustered_rowstore_indexes', fetch_result=True) -%}

    SELECT i.name AS index_name
    , i.name + '__dbt_backup' as index_new_name
    , COL_NAME(ic.object_id,ic.column_id) AS column_name
    FROM sys.indexes AS i
    INNER JOIN sys.index_columns AS ic
        ON i.object_id = ic.object_id AND i.index_id = ic.index_id and i.type <> 5
    WHERE i.object_id = OBJECT_ID('{{ relation.schema }}.{{ relation.identifier }}')

    UNION ALL

    SELECT  obj.name AS index_name
    , obj.name + '__dbt_backup' as index_new_name
    , col1.name AS column_name
    FROM sys.foreign_key_columns fkc
    INNER JOIN sys.objects obj
        ON obj.object_id = fkc.constraint_object_id
    INNER JOIN sys.tables tab1
        ON tab1.object_id = fkc.parent_object_id
    INNER JOIN sys.schemas sch
        ON tab1.schema_id = sch.schema_id
    INNER JOIN sys.columns col1
        ON col1.column_id = parent_column_id AND col1.object_id = tab1.object_id
    INNER JOIN sys.tables tab2
        ON tab2.object_id = fkc.referenced_object_id
    INNER JOIN sys.columns col2
        ON col2.column_id = referenced_column_id AND col2.object_id = tab2.object_id
    WHERE sch.name = '{{ relation.schema }}' and tab1.name = '{{ relation.identifier }}'

  {% endcall %}
  {{ return(load_result('list_nonclustered_rowstore_indexes').table) }}
{% endmacro %}

macro.dbt_sqlserver.sqlserver__get_catal.macro_sql:
{% macro sqlserver__get_catalog(information_schemas, schemas) -%}
    {% set query_label = get_query_options() %}
    {%- call statement('catalog', fetch_result=True) -%}
        {{ get_use_database_sql(information_schemas.database) }}
        with
        principals as (
            select
                name as principal_name,
                principal_id as principal_id
            from
                sys.database_principals {{ information_schema_hints() }}
        ),

        schemas as (
            select
                name as schema_name,
                schema_id as schema_id,
                principal_id as principal_id
            from
                sys.schemas {{ information_schema_hints() }}
        ),

        tables as (
            select
                object_id,
                name as table_name,
                schema_id as schema_id,
                principal_id as principal_id,
                'BASE TABLE' as table_type
            from
                sys.tables {{ information_schema_hints() }}
        ),

        tables_with_metadata as (
            select
                object_id,
                table_name,
                schema_name,
                coalesce(tables.principal_id, schemas.principal_id) as owner_principal_id,
                table_type
            from
                tables
            join schemas on tables.schema_id = schemas.schema_id
        ),

        views as (
            select
                object_id,
                name as table_name,
                schema_id as schema_id,
                principal_id as principal_id,
                'VIEW' as table_type
            from
                sys.views {{ information_schema_hints() }}
        ),

        views_with_metadata as (
            select
                object_id,
                table_name,
                schema_name,
                coalesce(views.principal_id, schemas.principal_id) as owner_principal_id,
                table_type
            from
                views
            join schemas on views.schema_id = schemas.schema_id
        ),

        tables_and_views as (
            select
                object_id,
                table_name,
                schema_name,
                principal_name,
                table_type
            from
                tables_with_metadata
            join principals on tables_with_metadata.owner_principal_id = principals.principal_id
            union all
            select
                object_id,
                table_name,
                schema_name,
                principal_name,
                table_type
            from
                views_with_metadata
            join principals on views_with_metadata.owner_principal_id = principals.principal_id
        ),

        cols as (

            select
                c.object_id,
                c.name as column_name,
                c.column_id as column_index,
                t.name as column_type
            from sys.columns as c {{ information_schema_hints() }}
            left join sys.types as t {{ information_schema_hints() }} on c.system_type_id = t.system_type_id
        )

        select
            DB_NAME() as table_database,
            tv.schema_name as table_schema,
            tv.table_name,
            tv.table_type,
            null as table_comment,
            tv.principal_name as table_owner,
            cols.column_name,
            cols.column_index,
            cols.column_type,
            null as column_comment
        from tables_and_views tv
        join cols on tv.object_id = cols.object_id
        where ({%- for schema in schemas -%}
            upper(tv.schema_name) = upper('{{ schema }}'){%- if not loop.last %} or {% endif -%}
        {%- endfor -%})

        order by column_index
        {{ query_label }}

        {%- endcall -%}

    {{ return(load_result('catalog').table) }}

{%- endmacro %}

{% macro standardize_date(column_name) %}
{% set col = "TRIM(" ~ column_name ~ ")" %}

    CASE
        WHEN {{ col }} LIKE '[A-Z][a-z][a-z][a-z]% __, ____'
            THEN TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }})

        WHEN {{ col }} LIKE '[A-Z][a-z][a-z] __, ____'
            THEN TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }})

        WHEN {{ col }} LIKE '__-__-____'
            AND TRY_CONVERT(INT, SUBSTRING({{ col }}, 4, 2)) > 12
            THEN TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }}, 110)

        WHEN {{ col }} LIKE '__-__-____'
            AND TRY_CONVERT(INT, LEFT({{ col }}, 2)) > 12
            THEN TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }}, 105)

        WHEN {{ col }} LIKE '____-__-__'
            THEN TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }})

        WHEN {{ col }} LIKE '____/__/__'
            THEN TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }})

        WHEN {{ col }} LIKE '__/__/____'
            AND TRY_CONVERT(INT, SUBSTRING({{ col }}, 4, 2)) > 12
            THEN TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }}, 101)

        WHEN {{ col }} LIKE '__/__/____'
            AND TRY_CONVERT(INT, LEFT({{ col }}, 2)) > 12
            THEN TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }}, 103)

        ELSE TRY_CONVERT(DATE, {{ col }}, 101)

    END

{% endmacro %}

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.
